sources.citation: Daniel T. Gilbert, Jane E. J. Ebert (2002). Decisions and revisions: The affective forecasting of changeable outcomes. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 82(4), 503-514.
sources.notes: Harvard University photography darkroom experiment (Study 1 & forecasting studies): students printed 2 favorite black-and-white photos and picked 1 to keep, either permanently or with a 5-day swap window. Although 66.3% preferred a reversible choice beforehand, students stuck with an unchangeable final print grew significantly happier with their photo than students given 5 days to swap.

sources.citation: Sheena S. Iyengar, Mark R. Lepper (2000). When choice is demotivating: Can one desire too much of a good thing? Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 79(6), 995-1006.
sources.notes: Classic gourmet jam tasting booth field experiment comparing 24 flavors vs 6 flavors: 30% of shoppers at the 6-jar table actually bought a jar, compared with only 3% at the 24-jar table (a 10-fold purchase drop under open choice overload).

sources.citation: Katharina Voigt, Carsten Murawski, Sebastian Speer, Stefan Bode (2019). Hard Decisions Shape the Neural Coding of Preferences. The Journal of Neuroscience, 39(4), 718-726.
sources.notes: Modern >=2015 human fMRI study proving that committing to a hard decision actively reshapes preference representations in the prefrontal cortex right as the choice closes.

sources.citation: Katharina Voigt, Carsten Murawski, Sebastian Speer, Stefan Bode (2020). Effective brain connectivity at rest is associated with choice-induced preference formation. Human Brain Mapping, 41(11), 3077-3088.
sources.notes: Modern >=2015 human fMRI dynamic causal modeling study mapping effective connectivity between anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) conflict detection and dorsolateral/ventromedial prefrontal cortex preference updating.

sources.citation: Amitai Shenhav, Mark A. Straccia, Jonathan D. Cohen, Matthew M. Botvinick (2014). Anterior cingulate engagement in a foraging context reflects choice difficulty, not foraging value. Nature Neuroscience, 17(9), 1249-1254.
sources.notes: Human fMRI evidence demonstrating that dorsal anterior cingulate cortex tracks unresolved choice conflict and alternative-comparison difficulty.

sources.citation: Alexander Chernev, Ulf Bockenholt, Joseph K. Goodman (2015). Choice overload: A conceptual review and meta-analysis. Journal of Consumer Psychology, 25(2), 333-358.
sources.notes: Meta-analysis across 99 observations clarifying boundary conditions: open/complex choices hurt satisfaction most when decision difficulty and attribute trade-offs are high, whereas clear prior preferences protect satisfaction.
